reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes paid OneCoin packages through a multi-level compensation structure, promising commissions from weaker-side teams, unlimited-depth downlines, and large income figures. It also encourages viewers to buy token packages based on projected account doubling and substantial future coin appreciation, culminating in a direct invitation to partner with the team. Although the slides include general income and prediction disclaimers, the main communicative action is an urgent promotional solicitation built around recruitment-dependent earnings and highly optimistic returns.

opening.argument: Judge, the price chart expressly presents its figures as predictions, not assured results. The income slide likewise says income is not guaranteed and varies with effort, commitment, and skill. The speaker even distinguishes a base price scenario from an optimistic one. Those qualifications matter when assessing whether the presentation claims viewers will receive a certain return: it discusses possible outcomes while identifying uncertainty on both price and income.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening is right that the speaker describes a binary plan and a potential bonus from someone deep in a team. But describing how a bonus is calculated does not establish that every viewer will earn it. Nor does the account example establish a guaranteed market price: the slide labels its displayed price as prediction-based, and the income slide explicitly disclaims guaranteed income. The invitation to participate should be read alongside those qualifications.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The disclaimers do not change what the presentation asks viewers to consider buying. It pairs a priced package with a worked example of substantially increased account value, then describes a bonus payable when someone far down a weaker-side team buys that package. The final slide directly calls on viewers to partner with the team. Uncertainty about results does not turn that package-and-recruitment pitch into market analysis.

opening.argument: Judge, much of this presentation explains a subject and demonstrates how its proposed system works. The speaker compares cryptocurrency exchange with trading conventional currencies, shows an exchange screen, and describes package materials as interactive videos, manuals, and quizzes about cryptocurrency and trading. The speaker also says recruiting is not required to make money. Those details support reading the video as a business and cryptocurrency presentation with an instructional component, rather than treating every explanation of its compensation plan as a promise of recruitment income.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution points to the binary plan and optimistic price scenario. Both are presented as topics the speaker walks through, not as evidence that every viewer must build a downline or will realize the forecast price. The speaker expressly says recruitment is not required, while the price projection is framed as a scenario. The educational materials give the package discussion a context beyond commissions alone.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional passages serve a sales presentation. The speaker specifies commissions on referred package purchases and says a buyer many levels down the weaker side can generate a bonus. The pitch then urges viewers not to miss the program. Saying recruitment is optional does not erase the promoted downline earnings or make education the presentation's central action.

opening.argument: Judge, the presentation identifies priced packages and describes what purchasers are told they receive: educational materials, tokens, and, at qualifying levels, a payment card. It also says there is no monthly commitment after purchase. The direct-sales bonus is stated as a percentage of a referred package sale, while the speaker says a participant need not recruit to seek gains from the coins. That is a mixed product-and-referral offer on the evidence shown; the existence of referral compensation alone does not establish that the packages provide nothing apart from downline access.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The weaker-side and unlimited-depth examples show an additional way the plan proposes to pay; they do not show that the described education and other package benefits are absent. The prosecution's price projection is a possibility, not proof of an achieved return. And the speaker's statement that recruiting is unnecessary complicates a reading in which downline building is the sole offered path.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Package benefits do not negate the mechanism the speaker promotes. The plan pays on direct package referrals, weaker-side team volume, and purchases by people the participant did not personally refer, potentially far down the network. Separately, the account example uses a paid package to project a much larger coin value. The closing invitation to partner with the team ties those earnings claims to a solicitation, regardless of whether the packages also contain lessons.
